reason: The core idea of using mild thermal annealing to induce partial short-range ordering in a PtPdRhRuIrOs HEA for ethanol oxidation directly restates the finding of P28, which showed that heat treatment of homogeneous Rh-based solid-solution alloy NPs introduced inhomogeneity and enhanced catalytic activity. The mechanism (d-band center modulation) and predicted outcome (higher current density, lower onset potential) are textbook concepts in electrocatalysis. The hypothesis does not combine multiple sources, transfer to a new alloy with justification, or propose a novel mechanism; it applies a known treatment to a different HEA without explaining why it should work there.
copied_elements: thermal annealing to introduce inhomogeneity in solid-solution alloy NPs
enhanced catalytic activity from dissimilar interfaces/domains
d-band center modulation tunes adsorption energetics
improved current density and lower onset potential as activity metrics
standard electrochemical characterization and falsification by performance comparison
